finding.title: Use a clock-skew-safe timestamp, not client clock, for notification_settings updated_at LWW field
finding.why: This client-computed timestamp becomes the payload's updated_at field pushed via enqueueNotificationSettings; core/sync/merge/notification_settings_merger.dart (outside this batch) parses remote['updated_at'] to arbitrate LWW. If two devices' clocks disagree, the device with the faster/wrong clock can push a stale settings change that looks 'newer' and wins over a genuinely newer change made on a correctly-clocked device, silently reverting the user's real edit with no error surfaced anywhere. Confirming the full blast radius requires reading the outbox-drain write path (outside this batch) to see whether it overwrites this field with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() before commit.
finding.recommendation: Confirm whether the write path already substitutes a server timestamp before commit; if not, do so, or route the push side through the same clock-skew arbitration MergeStore.remoteIsNewer already implements for the pull side.
acceptance_criteria: A sync test with an artificially-skewed local clock demonstrates the genuinely later settings write wins regardless of which device has the faster clock.

finding.title: Add ProviderContainer-based tests for core/preferences notifiers; replace the string-grep sentinel test; fix the misplaced/illegitimate profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart barrel import
finding.rule: AG-5 (test mirrors lib) + TQ-8 (weak/non-behavioral assertion) + Rule 2 (no unauthorized re-export barrels)
finding.why: hebrew_terms_sentinel_test.dart's only coverage of the IL-1 sentinel-guard mechanism is a test that reads preference_providers.dart off disk as text via a CWD-dependent File() probe and checks for the substring 'profileId == 0' — it passes whether or not UseHebrewTerms.build() actually preserves state, and would still pass if the guard were pasted into an unrelated function; it is also fragile since the two hardcoded relative paths break if the runner's CWD differs. Meanwhile 7 of the 9 non-generated files in lib/core/preferences/ (hebrew_date_preference.dart, nikud_preference.dart, text_display_preference.dart, transliteration_variant_preference.dart, profile_scoped_preference.dart, preference_providers.dart, and effectively profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart) have no test at their mirrored test/core/preferences/ path. profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart IS tested, but only via test/features/sync/domain/profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart, which imports the class through an unauthorized 2-line re-export barrel (lib/features/sync/domain/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart) instead of importing core/preferences/ directly — exactly the kind of extra re-export barrel Rule 2 prohibits. This organizational split is why this batch's readUseHebrewCalendar/HebrewDatePreference default-drift finding went uncaught: the two halves of the same invariant are tested, if at all, in disconnected files/directories.
finding.recommendation: Add test/core/preferences/{hebrew_date_preference,nikud_preference,text_display_preference,transliteration_variant_preference,profile_scoped_preference,preference_providers}_test.dart with real ProviderContainer-driven assertions. Replace hebrew_terms_sentinel_test.dart's source-grep sub-test with a ProviderContainer test that drives UseHebrewTerms through a real-id -> 0 -> real-id transition and asserts state is preserved. Delete lib/features/sync/domain/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart, repoint its one import at core/preferences/ directly, and move the test file to test/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart.
acceptance_criteria: Every lib/core/preferences/*.dart (excluding .g.dart) has a mirrored test/core/preferences/*_test.dart, per AG-5.
hebrew_terms_sentinel_test.dart no longer reads source files off disk; the sentinel-guard assertion drives real Notifier behavior through a ProviderContainer.
lib/features/sync/domain/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart (the re-export barrel) is deleted; grep -rn "export 'package:learning_tracker/core" lib/features/sync/ returns nothing for this symbol.

finding.title: Extract a shared no-op FirestoreGateway/PushPipeline fake — hand-duplicated stubs push tutored_pull_isolation_test.dart to 767 lines
finding.why: FirestoreGateway is a single 408-line, 30+-method interface (push/fetch/listen for every entity kind); PushPipeline is similarly broad. tutored_pull_isolation_test.dart spends lines 48-333 (_ChildDataGateway, 286 lines) and 336-456 (_NoPushPipeline, 121 lines) — over 400 of its 767 lines, more than half the file — hand-stubbing methods the tests never call, most just throwing StateError. That alone breaches the 400-line AG-3 cap by nearly 2x. write_tee_status_update_test.dart hits the identical wall from the other direction: _EmptyGateway (line 34) implements only 7 of the ~30 methods and falls back to a bare `super.noSuchMethod` (line 85) to dodge the rest — a different workaround for the same fat-interface pain. Per a repo-wide grep (context only, files outside this batch), the same `implements FirestoreGateway` duplication recurs in 20+ other test/sync files, so a shared fake pays off well beyond this batch.
finding.recommendation: Add a shared no-op base (e.g. test/helpers/fakes/no_op_firestore_gateway.dart, no_op_push_pipeline.dart) whose every method either no-ops or throws a consistent 'not stubbed' error, and have tutored_pull_isolation_test.dart / write_tee_status_update_test.dart extend it and override only the handful of methods each test actually exercises. Consider splitting FirestoreGateway by concern (push/fetch/listen, own-data/child-data) as a longer-term ISP fix.
acceptance_criteria: find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400' no longer lists tutored_pull_isolation_test.dart.
A shared no-op FirestoreGateway/PushPipeline fake exists under test/helpers/ and both files in this finding use it instead of hand-stubbing the full interface.

finding.title: Complete B18 in siyumim_timeline_and_lifetime_providers_test.dart to actually exercise the unmark-after-mark ledger conflict it documents

evidence.quote:
// Then unmark the same seder — FIRST-WRITE WINS per putIfAbsent,
// so the positive mark placed first takes priority.

finding.why: B18's name and inline comments describe adding a positive seder mark then an unmark entry for the same seder, asserting the 'first (positive) mark' wins per putIfAbsent. The actual ledgerEntries list (lines 1143-1156) contains only the single positive entry -- the unmark _fakeLedgerData call described in the comment was never written -- so B18 exercises nothing beyond a trivial single-entry seder expansion already covered by B17, under a misleading name. computeLearnedLeafRefs' putIfAbsent (builder) plus getEntriesByCurriculum/getEntriesByTrack's orderBy(desc(completedAt)) (DAO) together implement a real 'most-recent-ledger-action-wins' contract with no shared documentation and no runtime assertion tying the two together; only B18b tests the mirror direction (unmark first, mark second). A regression that flips either half of that contract (e.g. a new query path that forgets the desc ordering, or a putIfAbsent that becomes an overwrite) would silently make an old bulk-mark override a later intentional unmark, and nothing in this suite would catch the positive-first/unmark-second direction.
finding.recommendation: Add the described second _fakeLedgerData(..., entryScope: 'unmark_seder') entry after the positive one in B18 and assert the leaf remains learned (mirroring B18b's assertion in the opposite order); add a doc comment on computeLearnedLeafRefs stating the newest-first ordering precondition it relies on from callers.
acceptance_criteria: B18's ledgerEntries list contains both a positive seder entry and a corresponding unmark_seder entry, and the test fails if putIfAbsent semantics regress
computeLearnedLeafRefs doc comment states its ledgerEntries-must-be-newest-first-by-completedAt precondition

finding.title: Mirror scheduler's domain/projection tests under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection per AG-5
finding.why: There is no test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/ directory at all — the 4-file domain/projection/ module (overdue_projection.dart, overdue_schedule.dart, overdue_types.dart, projection.dart) is instead tested from files scattered loosely under test/features/scheduler/, including overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart which sits inside the unrelated data/repositories/ test directory despite importing only domain/projection/projection.dart. A contributor looking for 'the projection tests' at the standard mirrored path won't find them, and a future agent adding coverage for overdue_projection.dart risks not noticing this file already covers related ground.
finding.recommendation: Relocate the projection-only test files under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/ to match lib/features/scheduler/domain/projection/.
acceptance_criteria: overdue_from_elapsed_study_days_test.dart and the other projection-only test files (e.g. reorder_amnesty_test.dart, collapse_daf_tasks_test.dart if scoped to projection) live under test/features/scheduler/domain/projection/.
